Maya: heads up — bringing up HF model `hf/gpt-mini-open` via the HF->Redwood convert flow and our quant evals are failing. Token counts differ between the HF tokenizer and the converted one which seems to cascade into generation diffs during 4-bit quant runs. Example input: `\"Hello\u200B world\"` (contains a zero-width space). HF encode -> 3 tokens. Converted encoder -> 2 tokens. Has anyone seen ZWSP / normalization / byte-fallback issues like this?

Ajay: can you paste the small reproducible snippet + the `tokenizer.json` you converted? quick check: run the HF tokenizer locally using `tokenizers` to compare. e.g.:
```
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('hf_tokenizer.json').encode('Hello\u200B world').tokens)"
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('converted.json').encode('Hello\u200B world').tokens)"
```

Maya: pasted minimal output:
```
# hf_tokenizer.json
['Hello', '\u200B', ' world']  # HF (3 tokens)
# converted.json
['Hello', ' world']            # Redwood conversion (2 tokens)
```
Also seeing the quant eval (4-bit) MRR drop only when we use the converted tokenizer; native HF baseline is fine.

Sophia: my hunch: two orthogonal bits: unicode normalizer + byte-fallback/pre-tokenizer handling. HF tokenizers sometimes use an explicit normalizer (NFKC/NFC) and `add_prefix_space` semantics for chat-style models. If conversion drops the normalizer or collapses zero-width chars during byte fallback, you get token shifts.

Dana: also check `special_tokens_map` and `added_tokens` in the `config.json` — if a special token contains invisible chars or normalized variants, the converter may canonicalize them away. We saw this with the ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE marker in the xformer bringup last quarter.

token-bot: eval/quant/throughput-regression-2026-03-19 failed for run `hf/gpt-mini-open-4bit` — delta MRR: -2.3%. Linked: https://ci.redwood/example/run/482

Ajay: short actionable checklist: 1) run the two `tokenizers` commands above to isolate whether the converter dropped a normalizer. 2) Try `unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)` on input to see if HF was doing NFKC implicitly. 3) Make converter preserve the HF `normalizer` block (NFKC/NFC/compat). 4) Add a conversion flag `preserve_zero_width=true` or map ZWSP -> `<ZWSP>` as an explicit added token while onboarding.

Maya: reproducer and quick debug notes posted to the ticket INF-482. Sample manual fix that worked locally: run a small pre-normalize shim before tokenization: `s = s.replace('\u200B', '<ZWSP>')` and add `'<ZWSP>'` to `added_tokens` in the converted tokenizer. After that converted.encode(s) matches HF tokens. Not a permanent solution but good for the eval rerun.

Sophia: test snippet for the repo: 
```
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
import unicodedata
s = 'Hello\u200B world'
# option A: rely on normalizer
print('hf:', Tokenizer.from_file('hf_tokenizer.json').encode(s).tokens)
# option B: convert shim
s2 = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s).replace('\u200B','<ZWSP>')
print('shim:', Tokenizer.from_file('converted.json').encode(s2).tokens)
```
If that passes we can add a unit test under `redwood/tests/tokenizer_repro` and include the tiny sample.

Ajay: long-term we should: a) make the HF->Redwood converter preserve the `normalizer` section verbatim, b) add automated checks for invisible char tokenization (ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, NBSP), and c) add an opt-in `preserve_prefix_space` mapping so chat templates that rely on leading spaces don't break. I'll open a converter PR after reviewing INF-482.

Maya: OK I'll open a PR with the test + minimal shim + link to the failing eval. Assigning to @Ajay for review. Will include the tiny eval rerun. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
